_doc: Full course blueprint run: course_outline → course_compile_lessons (fans out child lesson runs) → course_stitch (concatenates the per-lesson MP4s + emits one chapter marker per lesson). The outline stage exercises a single LLM call; compile_lessons exercises orchestrator's ability to spawn + await child runs, which is the highest-risk piece because it crosses the run dispatcher boundary. The course_stitch assertion proves chapter markers are derived from the real per-lesson durations: a non-blank title per lesson and >=2 distinct start offsets (so the first is 0 and the second is the cumulative offset, not all-zero). `config_overrides.course_thumbnail:false` SUPPRESSES the AI cover (course_thumbnail StageSkips) so this scenario does not add a second GPU image-gen call beyond the per-slide lesson images already exercised here; the cover path is covered by unit + youtube-route tests and the best-effort thumbnail never gates the run.

brief.learning_objective: Identify the top 3 churn drivers in your data.
Apply the 3-move playbook to your top accounts.

_pixel_doc:
Media ACCEPTANCE probes on the delivered master (scripts/e2e_validate.py _MEDIA_CHECKS). Before these, this scenario proved a url was a non-blank string and nothing about the bytes behind it. `artifact_reachable` proves the object downloads and decodes; `audio_present` proves an audio stream exists AND is not digital silence (ffmpeg volumedetect mean/peak dBFS); `resolution` reads the ENCODED width/height, not the number the stage reports about itself; `stream_durations` measures the VIDEO and AUDIO stream durations SEPARATELY and never the container -- a container duration is the MAX over its streams, so it can never refute a truncated video track. Floors are the ones this scenario's existing green assertions already prove, never new tuning numbers.

`duration_within_tolerance` is present but DISARMED (`"enabled": false`). It compares the delivered stream length against `ordered_seconds` at the SAME +/-10% the pipeline's own duration_conformance uses. Flip `enabled` to true to arm it -- deliberately not armed while the duration calibration work is in flight, because a red instrument on known-in-flight work teaches people to ignore the instrument.

expect_pixel_checks._doc: Header-vs-packets guard on the delivered master. THE incident: an mp4 whose `moov` declared 12.0s over data that demuxed to 2.84s of picture. Every header-reading duration assertion reads that same claim -- in the recorded case `stream_durations` even saw a 0.00s A/V skew, because both numbers came from the one lying mux -- so a master whose picture stopped 9s early passed all of them. This is the only check that compares the DECLARED duration against the duration that actually demuxes (packet count / avg_frame_rate), which is what makes the disagreement visible. No thresholds are pinned here on purpose: the tolerance lives once, in scripts/e2e_validate.py.
